name: Brain and Cognitive Sciences
notes: Independent study courses (BCSC 391, BCS 395C) do not fulfill any major requirement.
The page notes students without CHEM 131 may struggle in BIOL 110 - advisory only.
STAT 212/213 were renamed STAT 180/190 per the Statistics program; both code families accepted.
A formal methods (statistics) course must be completed before taking a lab course - not auto-enforced.
BCSC 206/207 research sequence: both required; 207 fulfills the lab requirement, 206 may count as an elective.
Electives should form a coherent track (3 of 4 on-theme, at most one 100-level); allied fields should relate to the track - adviser-approved, not auto-enforced.

requirementGroups.label: Science foundation: biology
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: BIOL 110: Principles of Biology I; BIOL 112: Perspectives in Biology I

requirementGroups.label: Science foundation: calculus
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: MATH 141: Calculus I; MATH 161: Calculus IA; MATH 171: Honors Calculus I

requirementGroups.label: Science foundation: symbolic systems
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: LING 110: Introduction to Linguistic Analysis; CSC 173: Computation and Formal Systems; CSC 242: Artificial Intelligence

requirementGroups.label: Science foundation: programming
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Choose one of the following: CSC 161: Art of Programming; CSC 171: Science of Programming; BIOL 208: Intro to Programming for Biology

requirementGroups.label: BCS foundation and core
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: BCSC 110: Neural Foundations of Behavior; BCSC 111: Foundations of Cognitive Science; BCSC 151: Perception and Action; BCSC 152: Language and Psycholinguistics; BCSC 153: Cognition; BCSC 310: Senior Seminar

requirementGroups.label: Formal methods (statistics)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students are required to take STAT 212: Applied Statistics for Biological and Physical Sciences. Alternative statistics courses, such as STAT 211, STAT 213, STAT/BIOL 214, DSCC 262, PSYC/CSSP 211, and ECON 230, will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

requirementGroups.label: Laboratory course
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: One of the following: BCSC 204: Lab in Cognitive Neuroscience; BCSC 205: Lab in Development and Learning; BCSC 206/207: Undergraduate Research in Cognitive Science; BCSC 208: Lab in Perception and Cognition

requirementGroups.label: BCS upper-level electives (4, forming a track)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students are required to take four BCS elective courses. ... At least three of the four electives should adhere to the track theme. No more than one 100-level course may be used in the track.

requirementGroups.label: Allied fields (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must take two courses from the approved allied field courses list, which includes math, computer science, biology, chemistry, physics, philosophy, linguistics, optics, and engineering.
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: the approved list is department-maintained; this department filter is an approximation.

requirementGroups.label: Open electives (2)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students are required to take two elective courses, which can be additional BCS or allied field courses, or a combination of the two.

upperLevelWriting.label: Lab course + senior seminar
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Successful completion of the laboratory course and the senior seminar will satisfy the upper-level writing requirement.
